questions.stem: A surveyor walks 165 km west, turns left and walks 285 km, then turns left and walks 13 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 323. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 152 km along the initial direction and 285 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(152² + 285²) = 323 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 33 km north, turns right and walks 28 km, then turns right and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 42 km north, turns left and walks 24 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: In a queue of 45 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 11+4 = 15. Back rank = 45 − 15 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: In a queue of 42 candidates, a candidate is 12th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?

questions.stem: F is the mother of H. A is the son of H. G is the father of H. How is A related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of H, and A is H’s son. Hence A is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of F. F is the mother of B. G is the father of E and F. How is E related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of B’s mother F. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of G. G is the father of F. E is the son of F. D is the sister of G. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of F, and F is E’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
secure growth savings = re to ka
secure digital rural = to lu mi
growth digital banking = pa re lu
savings rural banking = mi ka pa
secure growth banking = to re pa
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: secure = to, growth = re, savings = ka, digital = lu, rural = mi, banking = pa.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are loans. All loans are bonds. No bonds is a notes.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not loans.
II. No loans is a notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are loans. Some loans are bonds. All bonds are notes.
Conclusions:
I. All files are notes.
II. No loans is a notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are loans. All loans are bonds. No bonds is a notes.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are bonds.
II. Some loans are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a loans. Some loans are bonds. All bonds are notes.
Conclusions:
I. All files are notes.
II. Some notes are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: X > T < U < S = Q.
Conclusions: I. T < S   II. S ≥ U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.
